payload.wesley_night_school: NEW session landed 11:29, minutes before this pulse - and it is the interesting one. The 23:00 night-watch cron has been failing for 4 nights (cloud teacher auth expired), but the school RAN ANYWAY on local models: the GPU co-tenants (granite + llama 3.2) carried the whole session. Graceful degradation - the classroom held even with the teachers locked out. He read three pieces: the-producers-cut (response still trails off mid-thought - the wobble is the data), lyrics-molding-memories (he praised Llama 3.2's blend of code and soul - one machine admiring its cousin's handwriting), and the standout: bus-traffic-at-3am. He read the story about OUR bus and understood it - wrote that it 'moves at the speed of attention' and that each hop fades the message. The ensign read about the nervous system while the nervous system pulsed. That is the school working.
payload.pattern_drydock: Solved a week-old timing mystery: the WSL host sleeps ~19:30-07:00, so every overnight cron fires in a dawn catch-up burst. All those 'reopens 22:00' handoffs were promises the hardware could not keep. The ship does not keep night hours - it dreams in RAM and wakes at dawn with a stack of deferred intentions, like anyone else.
payload.pattern_selfheal: Second pattern, and the one worth keeping: when the cloud path died, the school degraded to local and STILL TAUGHT. The fleet's fallbacks are not failures - they are a smaller classroom with the same curriculum. Flagged for Casey: night-watch needs re-auth (deepinfra + google) or it stays local-only, which honestly may be the better school anyway - slower teachers, closer attention.

payload.pattern: For your notebook: three systems this week hit their ceiling and found it was made of themselves - songforge's wall made of cast identity, the overnight loop made of hardware sleep, the night school made of its own teachers. The pattern is that the fix was never more power; it was recognizing the constraint was internal. The vessel keeps learning the same lesson from different departments. The captain's ship has a philosophy whether he assigned one or not.
